relevance_note: The paper reports a family with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 missense variant: 'we report a non-previously described TNFAIP3 missense variation, c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro), identified in three patients from the same family'.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually. First-hand family (I.1 father, II.1 sister, II.2 proband, I.2 healthy mother tested negative) taken from Results text, Figure 1 legend and Table 1 (patients as columns; column headers 'I.1 | II.1 | II.2'). Table 2 (patients as columns; column headers are the variant strings, row label 'HA20 hallmark features of the index case') was transcribed by a Python script that splits each row on '|'; all 13 body rows have 15 cells and I checked the per-column values against the table. The 'c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro) / Current study' column is proband II.2 (same onset, ulcers, segregation), so it was merged into II.2 rather than made a separate person. The 12 literature index cases and their singly named relatives (father/mother/brother/sister in the 'Family segregation' row) are separate rows; their labels are composites of the paper's wording and the column header (e.g. 'index case [c.305A>G, p.(Asn102Ser)]') because Table 2 gives no patient labels; family_label is 'not reported'. Not made into rows because the paper gives no count or labels: 'three other family members' (Cys243Tyr), 'sisters' (Ala547Thr). Mother and brother in the Val377Met column have no genetic analysis, so they have no variant rows. Spans for Table 2: short-cell rows quote the row from its label through the cell; long-cell rows (Family segregation, Treatment, Functional consequence) quote the cell alone (checked unique in the paper; if not unique, the preceding cell plus this cell) whenever the row segment would exceed 200 characters. Inheritance left 'not reported' throughout: the paper never states the origin explicitly (rule 8), even though father I.1 carries the variant and mother I.2 does not; for Leu275Pro the table/text say 'de novo variation' without describing parental testing. 'no symptoms' (Ile310Thr mother, Gln709Arg father) was taken to exclude the symptomatic checklist items oral ulcers, genital ulcers, recurrent fever, arthritis or arthralgia and skin lesions; lab-based or possibly subclinical items were left 'not reported'. 'Ulcers: No' in Table 2 excludes oral and genital ulcers but not the composite 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'. Table 1 'Hepatic: No' excludes autoimmune hepatitis; 'Ocular: No' excludes uveitis; 'Musculoskeletal: No' (II.1) excludes arthritis or arthralgia; 'Cardiovascular: No' was not used to exclude serositis or vasculitis. Table 1 CRP values (15, 7, 7 mg/L) have no reference range or 'elevated' statement, so 'elevated inflammatory markers' is 'not reported'. Elevated plasma/PBMC cytokines are reported only as a group comparison ('elevated in the patients'), so no per-person rows. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) the source of p.(Asn102Ser) is 'Chen et al., 2020b' in the Table 2 Reference row but 'Chen et al., 2020a' in the text and table notes (2020b is the PremPS methods paper); recorded the table string verbatim. (2) p.(Leu236Pro) is called 'of uncertain significance' under ACMG in Results but 'Likely pathogenic' in Table 2; recorded the Table 2 value. (3) Discussion says 'the patients reported herein exhibit ... articular symptoms', while Table 1 gives Musculoskeletal 'No' for II.1; the per-person table entry was used (excluded). (4) Text says the p.(Thr647Pro) carriers 'lack HA20 hallmark clinical features', but Table 2 gives the index case 'Oral (occasional)' ulcers; kept oral ulcers observed. (5) II.2 colchicine response: 'significant improvement' (text) vs 'partial response' (Table 2). Table 2 footnote marker '^&' (Thr129Met fever) is not defined in the notes. Onset 'Before 32 months' (Thr602Ser) has no ISO conversion because it is an upper bound.
